text:
jordan: Heads-up: promoted py/ts SDK 3.8.0 to GA in the 02:00 UTC quiet window. Seeing customer reports of 401s for refresh flow. Investigating.

deploy-bot: Promotion completed: jobs=[publish-py,publish-ts,tag-update]. Canary->GA. Metrics snapshot: auth_errors spiked from 0.02% to 1.5% in the last 5m.

pat: Oof. Which endpoints are 401ing? Any correlation with region or token type?

emma: A few reports pinned to customers on Dedicated region-eu-west-1 and using long-lived API keys. Error logs show "invalid_grant" during refresh.

alex: Quick telemetry: looks like the auth middleware was switched to prefer new KMS key name when migrating creds, and private deploys with old key binding get 401s. This is the change Sam mentioned in RC notes.

jordan: We need an immediate rollback. Rollback criteria hit (auth error >0.5% AND customer-facing failures). Procedure: swap dist-tags back (npm: latest->3.7.4, rc->3.8.0-rc1; pip: stable->3.7.4). Also trigger hotfix branch and start 3.8.1-hotfix build.

deploy-bot: Initiating dist-tag swap and canary revert. Actions: 1) set npm dist-tag latest=3.7.4 2) set npm dist-tag rc-3.8.0=3.8.0-rc1 3) pip release pointer updated to 3.7.4 4) rollback K8s deployment -> previous replicaSet.

pat: I'll run the npm tag swap: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@3.7.4 latest` then `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@3.8.0-rc1 rc-3.8.0`

emma: I'm reverting the wheels in the artifact registry and restoring the pip pointer in the publish metadata. Will post PR tags.

support-bot: Alerting customers on watchlist: messages queued -> 12 customers. Template prepared: "We're rolling back SDK 3.8.0 due to auth regressions affecting token refresh on some private deployments. Next steps: we'll publish a hotfix with reverted KMS lookup within 2 hours."

alex: Root cause short: publish script accidentally flipped a config flag `KMS_USE_NEW_KEY=true` in the runtime image for GA build. RC builds were fine. Need to update the publish pipeline to decouple runtime image config from dist-tag promotion.

jordan: Assign owners: @alex root-cause + patch. @pat run dist-tag swaps now. @emma coordinate hotfix branch and trigger CI. @support-bot send customer msgs.

deploy-bot: Dist-tag swap complete. NPM latest -> 3.7.4. Pip pointer restored. GA endpoints rolled back to previous replicaSet. Canary->reverted.

pat: Confirmed: `npm dist-tag ls @redwood/sdk` shows latest: 3.7.4, next: 3.8.0-rc1. Pulled a fresh install to verify: client auth refresh back to expected behavior locally.

emma: Hotfix branch created: release/hotfix-3.8.1. Patch change: revert KMS flag and add explicit env guard. Running CI now.

alex: Also adding a post-publish smoke job that runs auth-refresh against staging before swapping dist-tags. PR coming.

deploy-bot: CI for hotfix build -> running. Unit tests passed, integ-tests queued.

jordan: Good. Two more follow-ups before re-promote: (1) add migration note to release notes clarifying KMS change and recommended customer action if pinned, (2) add canary smoke gate to publish pipeline.

support-bot: Customer comms sent for initial rollback: 12 messages queued -> sent successfully. Slack DM to oncall-sre with incident link.

pat: Once hotfix CI green, we'll publish 3.8.1 as `hotfix`/`latest`? My vote: publish hotfix under rc tag first, run 1h canary with auth smoke, then promote to latest and npm/pip stable. Keep a manual hold for 30m after promotion.

emma: Agree. Plan: publish 3.8.1-rc1 under rc tag, canary 5% for 1h, run `auth-smoke` + `e2e-refresh`. If green -> swap dist-tags and announce GA. If failing -> rollback again and open a postmortem.

alex: I'll also add telemetry annotation for the GA promotion event so we can correlate client version -> errors quickly in future.

jordan: Thanks all. Documenting the timeline in the playbook and filing a short incident ticket for postmortem. Closing this thread; continuing hotfix work in release/hotfix-3.8.1 PR.

emma: ack, moving to PR.

pat: ack.

deploy-bot: CI hotfix -> success. Artifact published: @redwood/sdk@3.8.1-rc1. Canary started (5%).

support-bot: Notifying watchlist that hotfix canary is live.

jordan: Leaving watch on observability for the next 1h. Please ping here on any auth anomalies.
